transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well... I guess what finally scared me enough to make an appointment is that I just keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. It's just this heavy thought I can't shake. And... sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic, I actually catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the steering wheel. That really frightened me, so... that's why I'm here.

Have you ever had periods lasting several days or longer where your mood was unusually high or expansive, where you felt like you could do anything, needed very little sleep, and your thoughts were racing?

Well, yes. Earlier this month, actually. I had a few days where I felt almost... electrically upbeat, I guess you could say. But it turned into me just snapping at everyone over really tiny things. Like, if a medication cup was misplaced at the clinic, or if there was a minor change in our morning schedule, I would just lose my temper. It really didn't feel like my usual self at all.

During that electrically upbeat period earlier this month, did you experience anything unusual like hearing voices, seeing things, or believing things that others didn't seem to believe—even if just for a moment?

No, nothing like that. I didn't hear any voices or see anything that wasn't there. I didn't have any strange beliefs, either. I was just... really wired and angry, like I said. But my mind wasn't playing tricks on me or anything.

You mentioned feeling that heavy thought about not waking up and those intrusive thoughts while driving—are you still having those thoughts right now, or did they happen mainly during that 'electrically upbeat' period you described?

Oh, no, I'm having them right now. During that upbeat period earlier this month, I didn't feel this way at all—I was just really irritable and wired. The thoughts about not waking up, or the steering wheel... those are happening now. They've been pretty constant lately, which is why I'm sitting here today.

When did these thoughts about not waking up and the intrusive thoughts while driving first start—was that before the 'electrically upbeat' period earlier this month, or did they begin after that period ended?

They started way before that upbeat period. Honestly, this heavy feeling... it's been hanging over me for about 11 months now. It's just that recently, after that wired phase ended, everything shifted and it's become completely unbearable. But yeah, the depression itself has been there for almost a year.

You mentioned the depression has been going on for about 11 months, and the wired, irritable period happened earlier this month. So just to be clear: was there a time when you felt normal or okay between when the depression started 11 months ago and when you had that wired period earlier this month, or has the heavy depressed feeling been pretty much continuous this whole time?

No, there hasn't really been a break. It's just been one long stretch of feeling like this for the past 11 months. The only time it felt different was during those few days earlier this month when I got so wired and angry, but otherwise, yeah, it's just been a continuous heavy feeling the whole time.

During that wired and irritable period earlier this month, did you do things that were risky or that you wouldn't normally do—like spending a lot of money impulsively, taking on major projects, or engaging in other behaviors that had real consequences?

Yeah, I did. I work as a vet tech, and during that wired stretch, I just... I got it in my head that I needed all this stuff for the clinic and for some rescues I foster. I bought all this monitoring equipment, um, ramps, specialized bedding, just... a bunch of supplies. It wasn't planned. It just felt urgently necessary right then, like I had to have it all immediately. I just put it all on my credit card. It was only after that phase ended that I looked at the statement and realized I'd racked up charges that my husband and I really can't cover.

During that wired period earlier this month when you were so irritable and energetic, did you feel like your thoughts were moving so fast that you couldn't keep up with them, or did you jump from topic to topic in a way that others had trouble following?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my thoughts were definitely racing a bit, just because I was so agitated and focused on getting all those supplies, but I didn't feel like I couldn't keep up with them. And my husband didn't say anything about me not making sense or jumping around when I talked. I was just really intense and irritable about everything.

During these 11 months when you've been feeling that heavy depressed feeling, have you ever experienced any hallucinations, heard voices, or had beliefs that others didn't share—even if you knew they didn't make complete sense?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. It's really just been the heavy, exhausted feeling and the lack of motivation. My thoughts have been pretty grounded in reality, just... very negative.

During these 11 months of feeling heavy and depressed, have you had any beliefs about yourself—like thinking you're worthless, or that bad things are your fault, or that you deserve to suffer—that feel absolutely true to you, even though you know logically they might not be?

Yeah, I have. Um... I just keep telling myself I'm a terrible person. We've had some disruption at home lately, and I just resent it so much, which makes me feel incredibly guilty. I keep replaying every impatient look I've given my husband, or any sharp comment I've made, and it just... it feels like proof that he and the rest of the family would be better off without me. I know it sounds harsh, but that's just how it feels.

During these 11 months when you've been feeling depressed and heavy, have there been any times when you felt like your thoughts or perceptions were distorted in some way—like feeling disconnected from your body, or experiencing things in a strange or unreal way, even if just briefly?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. Um... I definitely don't feel disconnected from my body. If anything, I just feel really weighed down by it. But no, I haven't had any moments where things seemed strange or unreal to me. Everything feels very real, just... really bleak.

During those 11 months when you've been feeling depressed and heavy, were there any times when you believed things about yourself or the world that felt absolutely real to you at the time, but that you now recognize didn't make sense—like feeling like you had special powers, or that people were against you, or that you had done something terribly wrong that you actually hadn't?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean, like I said, I definitely feel guilty and think I'm a burden, but I don't think I have special powers or that anyone is plotting against me. It's just the guilt and the sadness, nothing bizarre or out of touch with reality.

During these 11 months when you've been feeling so depressed and guilty, have you ever believed that you've committed a serious crime or done something so terrible that you deserve to be punished or that you should be dead—beliefs that felt completely true even though there's no actual evidence for them?

No, I've never thought I committed a crime or anything like that. I mean, I feel terrible about how I act sometimes, and I definitely feel like they'd be better off if I wasn't here, but I don't think I've done something illegal or that I deserve to be punished in some official way. It's just... I just feel like a bad person, not a criminal.

During these 11 months when you've been feeling depressed, have there been times when you felt so guilty or ashamed that you believed you should be dead or that everyone would be better off without you—and did those beliefs feel absolutely certain and true, even if part of you knew they might not be logical?

Well, like I mentioned a minute ago, I definitely have those thoughts that my family would be better off without me. Just because I feel like such a burden to them right now. And I do think about not being here. But... I wouldn't say it feels like some absolute certainty that ignores logic. 

I mean, deep down I know they love me and wouldn't actually be better off. It's just... the guilt is so heavy that it's hard to focus on the logical part. So, no, I don't have those kinds of completely illogical beliefs, it's just a really overwhelming feeling of being useless.

Right now, as you're experiencing these heavy depressed feelings and thoughts about not waking up, are you also feeling irritable or angry—like you were during that wired period earlier this month—or is the irritability gone and it's mainly just the sadness and heaviness you're dealing with now?

Right now, no, the irritability is mostly gone. It's just... heavy. But earlier this month, yeah, I felt almost... electrically upbeat for a bit, and then I would just snap at everyone over the tiniest things. Like, at work, if someone misplaced a medication cup or if the morning schedule changed even a little bit, I would just lose it. It didn't feel like me at all. But right now, it's just the sadness.

During these 11 months of feeling depressed and guilty, have there been times when you believed something about yourself that felt absolutely, completely true—like that you had committed an unforgivable sin, or that you were evil or corrupt in some fundamental way, or that you deserved severe punishment—even though you can now see those beliefs didn't match reality?

No, I haven't ever believed I was evil or committed an unforgivable sin or anything extreme like that. It's more just... this constant, heavy guilt. 

I keep telling myself I'm a terrible person because I resent how much disruption there is at home right now. I just sit there and replay every impatient look I've given, or every sharp comment I've made, and I use it as proof that my husband and my family would just be better off without me. But it's not some delusion about being fundamentally corrupt or needing severe punishment. It's just me feeling completely worthless because of how I'm acting towards the people I love.

During that wired and irritable period earlier this month, did you need significantly less sleep than usual—like feeling rested after only 2-3 hours of sleep—or were you sleeping normally but just feeling too energized to want to sleep?

Yeah, I definitely needed a lot less sleep. During that high-energy stretch earlier this month, I was only sleeping maybe three hours a night. But the weird thing was, I'd still wake up before sunrise feeling completely sharp and ready to go. I honestly was convinced I just didn't need more rest than that.

During that wired and irritable period earlier this month when you were so energized and shopping impulsively, did you ever feel like your thoughts were so fast or so powerful that they felt like they were being put into your head by something outside of yourself, or did you ever feel like you had any special insight or understanding that other people didn't have?

No, nothing like that. My thoughts were definitely moving fast, like one idea crashing into the next, but they were my own thoughts. I didn't feel like anyone else was putting them there. And I didn't think I had any kind of special insight or anything... I just felt really energized and like I needed to get a million things done right then.

During these 11 months when you've been feeling so depressed and thinking that your family would be better off without you, have you ever actually heard voices—maybe a voice telling you that you're worthless, or commenting on what you're doing—even if you knew it wasn't really there?

No, I haven't heard any voices. It's just my own thoughts... my own voice in my head telling me those things, not anyone else's. I've never heard anything outside of myself or heard voices talking to me.

I mean, deep down I know they love me and wouldn't actually be better off. It's just... the guilt is so heavy that it's hard to focus on the logical part. So, no, I don't have those kinds of completely illogical beliefs, it's just a really overwhelming feeling of being useless.

doctor.question: During these 11 months of feeling depressed and guilty, have there been times when you believed something about yourself that felt absolutely, completely true—like that you had committed an unforgivable sin, or that you were evil or corrupt in some fundamental way, or that you deserved severe punishment—even though you can now see those beliefs didn't match reality?

patient.answer:
No, I haven't ever believed I was evil or committed an unforgivable sin or anything extreme like that. It's more just... this constant, heavy guilt. 

I keep telling myself I'm a terrible person because I resent how much disruption there is at home right now. I just sit there and replay every impatient look I've given, or every sharp comment I've made, and I use it as proof that my husband and my family would just be better off without me. But it's not some delusion about being fundamentally corrupt or needing severe punishment. It's just me feeling completely worthless because of how I'm acting towards the people I love.
